title: Drawing with canvas
objective: Draw rectangles, circles and lines on a canvas; draw a picture from an array with a loop
story: You've landed on Pixel Planet! Everything here is made of tiny colored dots: pixels. Today you'll draw with code on a drawing surface called **canvas** and draw the first picture of the play field.

sections.title: Canvas and brush
Coordinates: y grows downwards
sections.body:
Every point on the canvas has an `(x, y)` address. **The top-left corner is `(0, 0)`**. `x` grows to the right, and `y` grows **downwards** (the opposite of math class!).

| Point | x | y |
|---|---|---|
| Top-left corner | 0 | 0 |
| Top-right corner | 300 | 0 |
| Bottom-left corner | 0 | 200 |
| Middle | 150 | 100 |

So to move something up, you **decrease** `y`.

sections.title: Rectangles, outlines and the eraser
sections.body:
Choose the color first, then draw. `fillStyle` affects every fill drawing after it:

```js
ctx.fillStyle = "#0b1026";       // fill color
ctx.fillRect(0, 0, 300, 200);    // x, y, width, height

ctx.strokeStyle = "#f7df1e";     // line color
ctx.lineWidth = 3;
ctx.strokeRect(20, 20, 60, 40);  // an empty outline

ctx.clearRect(0, 0, 300, 200);   // erases the area (makes it transparent)
```

You can write colors as hexadecimal (hex) codes like `"#f7df1e"` or as names like `"white"`. A rectangle's `(x, y)` point is its **top-left corner**.

sections.title: Circles, lines, text and drawing from data

examples.title: Night scene
examples.note: Change the coordinates: to move the rocket right change x, to move it up decrease y.

examples.title: A sky from data
examples.note: The stars are in different places every time. Add a new planet to the planets array.

tasks.title: Space background
tasks.prompt:
Paint **the whole** `#c` canvas dark navy (`#0b1026`). Then draw a red (`#e53935`) rectangle on top, starting at `(20, 30)`, 60 wide and 40 high.

Don't type the canvas size yourself: use `canvas.width` and `canvas.height`.
hints: The whole canvas: ctx.fillRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
Then change the color and ctx.fillRect(20, 30, 60, 40);

tasks.title: Orange planet
tasks.prompt: Draw an orange (`#ff9800`) **circle** with its center at `(100, 60)` and a radius of `30`. Use `beginPath`, `arc` and `fill`.
hints: ctx.arc(x, y, radius, 0, Math.PI * 2) describes a full circle.
First ctx.beginPath(), at the end ctx.fill().

tasks.title: Draw the stars from an array
tasks.prompt:
Write the `drawStars()` function:

1. First it clears the whole canvas with `clearRect`.
2. Then for every star in the `stars` array it draws a 10×10 yellow (`#f7df1e`) square starting at `(x, y)`.

When the array changes and `drawStars()` is called again, the picture should change too.
hints: for (const star of stars) { ctx.fillRect(star.x, star.y, 10, 10); }

challenge.title: Chessboard
challenge.prompt:
Draw an 8×8 chessboard on the `#board` canvas. Each square is 20×20 pixels.

- If the sum of the row and column numbers is **even**, the square is white (`#ffffff`); if it's **odd**, it's dark (`#1b1f33`).
- Use two nested `for` loops: one for the rows (`row`), one for the columns (`col`).
- A square starts at `(col * 20, row * 20)`.
challenge.starter:
const ctx = document.querySelector("#board").getContext("2d");

// 64 squares with two nested loops
hints: for (let row = 0; row < 8; row++) { for (let col = 0; col < 8; col++) { ... } }

project_task.title: Play field
project_task.prompt:
Time to draw Star Hunter's play field! Write the `drawGame()` function:

1. Paint the whole canvas `#0b1026` (this also erases the old picture).
2. Draw the ship as a blue (`#4fc3f7`) rectangle using the `x`, `y`, `w`, `h` values in the `ship` object.
3. Draw every star in the `stars` array as a yellow (`#f7df1e`) circle with its center at `(x, y)` and a radius of `6`.

When the ship or the stars change and `drawGame()` is called again, the picture should change too.
hints: For every star: beginPath, arc(star.x, star.y, 6, 0, Math.PI * 2) and fill.
